questions.sub: Ancient India: Indus Valley, Vedic period, Mauryas, Guptas
questions.question: Which Indus Valley Civilization site is famous for the discovery of the 'Great Bath'?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath, a large public water tank likely used for ritual bathing, was discovered at Mohenjo-daro.

questions.sub: Ancient India: Indus Valley, Vedic period, Mauryas, Guptas
questions.question: The Mauryan emperor who embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and propagated Dhamma through edicts is:
questions.explanation: Emperor Ashoka, after the bloodshed of the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE), converted to Buddhism and spread the message of Dhamma through his edicts.

questions.sub: Medieval India: Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, Bhakti and Sufi movements
questions.question: Who founded the Delhi Sultanate by establishing the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty in 1206?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a former slave-general of Muhammad Ghori, founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty in Delhi in 1206, marking the start of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.sub: Medieval India: Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, Bhakti and Sufi movements
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor is credited with building the Taj Mahal at Agra?
questions.explanation: Emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, completed around 1653.

questions.sub: Advent of Europeans and British expansion
questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757), which laid the foundation of British political power in India, was fought between the British East India Company and:
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between Robert Clive's forces and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, resulting in a decisive British victory.

questions.question: The Revolt of 1857 began at which cantonment town, sparked by the issue of greased cartridges?
questions.explanation: The Revolt of 1857 broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, after sepoys refused to use cartridges rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat.

questions.question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a pioneer of socio-religious reform who campaigned against Sati, founded which organisation in 1828?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 in Calcutta, campaigning against practices like Sati and for social reform.

questions.sub: Indian National Congress and moderates vs extremists
questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with which person as its first President?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in December 1885.

questions.sub: Gandhian movements: Non-cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India
questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with which act of defiance?
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement with the Dandi Salt March (Salt Satyagraha) from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, beginning 12 March 1930, defying the salt tax law.

questions.sub: Gandhian movements: Non-cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India
questions.question: The Quit India Movement, with the slogan 'Do or Die', was launched by Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 after the All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India Resolution in Bombay.

questions.question: Who founded the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) revolutionary movement and led it during the Second World War with Japanese support?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose reorganised and led the Indian National Army (INA/Azad Hind Fauj) from 1943, seeking to liberate India with Japanese assistance during WWII.

questions.question: India attained independence and was partitioned into India and Pakistan under which Act of the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, provided for the partition of British India into two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, effective 15 August 1947.

questions.question: The integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union after independence was principally overseen by:
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, as Home Minister and head of the States Department, along with V. P. Menon, masterminded the integration of princely states into the Indian Union.
